name: First Fort Dearborn — the interpreter's house

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: THE RANGE IS INFERRED, NOT DATED FOR THIS BUILDING. It opens on 25 January 1808, the date Whistler's draught carries, which is the one day on which a source shows it standing. It may well be older. It closes on 16 August 1812 with the first fort, the day after the evacuation, when the post was burned (data/exclusions.json fort_dearborn_first_1803). No source in the corpus says the buildings outside the stockade burned with it. Closing them with the fort is the conservative reading: it keeps them out of every later scene and adds nothing to one.

placement.position_note: PLACED BY T-2062's RULE, NOT MEASURED. The draught says the buildings outside the garrison are 'not laid down by a scale', so this box is the sheet's ARRANGEMENT opened out about the main gate. The sheet box is px [411, 1219, 491, 1266]. Its offset from the gate's mouth (px [964, 1150]) is multiplied by 3.322, the ratio of the drafter's 'Distance to Main Gate Eighteen Perches' (297 ft) to the 89 ft the sheet draws for the agent's house. The rule and its numbers are data/traces/whistler_1808_fort_dearborn.json § outside_the_stockade, and tools/read_whistler_1808.py --check (run by check.sh) refuses this point if it is not what the rule gives, to 0.01 m, and refuses any footprint corner on the committed 1812 water. Seated with the fort's own frame: the staff's foot at local E +1152, N +221, the frame's north on grid north. The rule is a reconstruction (docs/LIBERTIES.md L391, L-T2507). THE FIGURE THAT DOES NOT GOVERN: this house's own 'Distance to the Main Gate is fortyeight Perches' (792 ft, 6.9 times the drawing) would seat it with a footprint corner 0.4 m inside the committed 1812 river, so it takes no. 17's 3.3 instead (expansions.interpreter_19). The drawing is turned about 32 degrees off the sheet's axes, and the record is turned with it (turn_deg -32, front to bearing 148).
placement.symbolic_location: Outside the first Fort Dearborn, in the frame of Whistler's 1808 draught (T-2507, by T-2062's rule, part 'interpreters_house'): E -402.7..-367.3 ft, N -135.0..-114.2 ft of the flagstaff's foot, facing south-south-east (bearing 148); this record's origin is the box's corner the seat names for that facing, turned with the drawing about the box's centre.

footprint.note: THE DRAWN BOX AT FORTY FEET TO THE INCH, the scale the index states for the Indian Department's dwellings, as for the agent's house. The drawing is a small pictorial elevation, roof and front together, so the plan is an upper bound and is reconstructed.

stories.note: The draught draws its front with two rows of two lights, as it draws the agent's two-storey house.

wall_height_m.note: Unattested. Two storeys of hewn log, about fifteen feet to the eaves, as the agent's house.

construction.note: Unattested. Log, like the factor's and the agent's houses Quaife calls 'two log houses'.

roof_type.note: The draught draws a pitched roof behind the front, to the north-north-west.

roof_pitch_deg.note: Unattested; the draught's pictorial roof gives no pitch.

loft.note: Two full storeys, so no loft is modelled.

chimneys.note: Marks at both ends of the drawn roof may be stacks, as the agent's house's are; at this size they are not read with confidence.

function.note: Index no. 19, 'Interpreters House': the house the draught gives the post's interpreter, west-south-west of the fort. Who lived in it in 1812 is not read: Surgeon Cooper (Quaife 1913, as T-2504 quotes him) puts La Lime, the interpreter, in one of the four houses north of the river in 1808, and La Lime was killed in the spring of 1812. Nobody is placed in it (L1).

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 1. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1884.

Whistler, Captain John. "Fort Dearborn" [draught of the garrison and its vicinity], dated in the parade 'January 25th 1808', with its 'Index annexed to the Draught of Fort Dearborn &c.' signed at Fort Dearborn 20 February 1808. Original in the files of the War Department, Washington. Reproduced as the plate 'Fort Dearborn and Vicinity in 1808. From the original draft by Captain Whistler in the archives of the War Department at Washington', facing p. 164 of Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835 (Chicago, 1913); the index is printed in full in note 413 on the same pages.
what_it_supplies: the first fort's garrison in plan at a stated scale: the double row of pickets, the two blockhouses at the north-west and south-east angles, the four barracks ranges, the magazine, two small houses, the main gate, the parade and the flagstaff
the drafter's index of 34 numbered features, and the note that two of them (the covered way and the gutters) are omitted from their places
the arrangement of the factor's and agent's establishments, stables, gardens and the houses across the river, by position only and not to scale
what_it_does_not_supply: any building height: the folded elevations disagree with each other
the fort's bearing to true north: no north arrow was found on the reproduction
the covered way to the river and the gutters, which the index itself says are omitted
anything about the second fort of 1816

research_note: THE INTERPRETER'S HOUSE, no. 19, the one house on Whistler's sheet drawn turned. Its own stated distance, 48 perches, would put it in the 1812 river, so it stands by no. 17's figure (T-2507). Nobody is placed in it (L1).
